_readme: Everything here can be edited without touching code. Keep the same shape: change the words and numbers, not the names on the left. After editing, the app picks it up next time it's started.

help.disclaimer: This program supports self-help and is not a substitute for professional care.

services.name: Gambling Help Online
services.detail: Free and confidential, 24/7, phone and live chat

services.name: Emergency
services.detail: If you or someone else is in danger right now

insight.title: Urges fade the less you feed them
insight.text: An urge can feel like it'll last forever, but most rise, peak and pass within about half an hour. Every time you ride one out, the next one tends to be a bit easier. Week 4 is all about this.

goals.label: Cut back
goals.detail: Gamble less and stay in control

insight.title: Decide your limits before, not during
insight.text: Limits made in the moment rarely hold, because gambling is built to keep you going. Limits you set ahead of time, with money and time agreed up front, work much better. We'll help you set yours.

goals.label: Take a break
goals.detail: Step away for a while and see how it feels

insight.title: A break shows you what's changed
insight.text: Stepping away for a while is a chance to notice what's different: your money, your sleep, your mood, how much head space you've got. You decide what comes next once you've seen it.

goalFallback.title: A break shows you what's changed
goalFallback.text: Stepping away for a while is a chance to notice what's different: your money, your sleep, your mood, how much head space you've got. You decide what comes next once you've seen it.

insight.title: Pokies are built to keep you playing
insight.text: Every spin is random, so a win is never 'due', and over time the machine always comes out ahead. The lights and sounds even celebrate 'wins' smaller than your bet, so losing can feel like winning.

insight.title: The apps are designed around the game
insight.text: In-play bets, multis and 'bonus bets' keep you tapping while the game is on. Knowing a sport well doesn't change the fact that the prices are set so the bookmaker comes out ahead.

insight.title: A race every few minutes
insight.text: With races running back to back all day, there's always another chance to win it back. That constant next one is what makes it so hard to stop at a set amount.

insight.title: Always open, money that doesn't feel real
insight.text: Online games never close, and money on a screen doesn't feel like cash in your hand. That makes it easy to lose track of time and spend more than you meant to.

insight.title: Small amounts add up quietly
insight.text: Because each ticket is cheap and everyday, it's easy to miss how much it adds up to over a month or a year. Tracking it is often an eye-opener.

insight.title: Fast games, quick decisions
insight.text: A new game every few minutes means there's little time to stop and think between bets. Slowing things down is one of the most useful skills you'll practise.

insight.title: The house edge never sleeps
insight.text: Every table game is set up so the casino comes out ahead over time. A good night doesn't change that. It just makes the next visit more tempting.

insight.title: Skill can make it harder to stop
insight.text: When skill plays a part, it's easy to believe you'll win it back next time. Chasing losses is one of the biggest thinking traps, and Week 3 covers it.

insight.title: Whatever it is, the hooks are similar
insight.text: Most gambling works the same way on the brain: uncertain wins, near misses and the chance to win it back. What you learn here applies to all of it.

gamblingTypesFallback.title: Whatever it is, the hooks are similar
gamblingTypesFallback.text: Most gambling works the same way on the brain: uncertain wins, near misses and the chance to win it back. What you learn here applies to all of it.

insight.title: The people closest to you notice first
insight.text: Gambling often hits family hardest: the time it takes, the money, the worry. The good news is they usually notice the change when things get better too. Week 5 covers rebuilding trust.

insight.title: The people closest to you notice first
insight.text: Gambling often hits family hardest: the time it takes, the money, the worry. The good news is they usually notice the change when things get better too. Week 5 covers rebuilding trust.

insight.title: Kids notice more than we think
insight.text: Kids pick up on stress, distraction and money worries, even when nobody says anything. More time and attention for them is one of the best things you'll get back.

insight.title: We'll keep count of what you keep
insight.text: Each week we'll show an estimate of the money you've kept and how close you are to your goal. Seeing it grow is a strong reason to keep going.

insight.title: Gambling and stress feed each other
insight.text: Gambling can mess with sleep, appetite and stress levels, and stress makes urges stronger. Looking after one helps the other.

insight.title: You're not alone with this
insight.text: Gambling problems often go hand in hand with feeling low or anxious. This program can help, and if things feel heavy, talking to someone helps too. Help is always one tap away.

insight.title: Keep your goal where you can see it
insight.text: People who keep their goal in front of them stick with change more often. We'll remind you of it on the tough days.

insight.title: Gambling takes more than money
insight.text: Lost sleep, checking apps and worrying about losses all eat into your focus at work. Getting that head space back is a real win.

insight.title: Control comes back bit by bit
insight.text: Every urge you ride out, every day you stick to your plan, builds the feeling that you're the one calling the shots again.

whyFallback.title: Your reason is your anchor
whyFallback.text: Whatever brought you here, hang on to it. On the tough days, remembering why you started is one of the most powerful tools you've got.

insight.title: Free time needs a plan
insight.text: Long stretches with nothing planned leave room for urges. Filling weekends with things you enjoy is part of Week 5.

insight.title: Tired brains find it harder to say no
insight.text: At the end of a long day, willpower runs low. A simple evening routine can take the pressure off.

insight.title: Plan payday before it arrives
insight.text: Having money land in your account is a big trigger. Sorting bills and savings first thing on payday, before anything else, makes a real difference. Week 2 shows you how.

insight.title: Sport and betting have been tied together
insight.text: Betting ads and in-game offers are built around the game you're watching. It's possible to enjoy the footy without them. Week 2 helps you plan for it.

insight.title: Alcohol loosens your limits
insight.text: A few drinks make it harder to stick to decisions you made sober. Planning ahead for nights out is one of the simplest ways to protect your progress.

insight.title: The urge is often about the feeling
insight.text: When you're stressed, gambling can feel like an escape. Often the urge isn't really about gambling, it's about wanting a break from the feeling. Week 4 gives you other ways to get that break.

insight.title: Boredom is a real trigger
insight.text: Gambling gives a quick buzz when life feels flat. Finding other things that give you a lift is a big part of Week 5.

insight.title: Being alone makes it easier to slip
insight.text: With no one around, there's nothing to interrupt the urge. Having someone to message, or something to do, can break the pattern.

riskyFallback.title: Knowing your triggers is half the battle
riskyFallback.text: Most people find the urge shows up at the same kinds of times. Over the next few weeks you'll learn to spot yours and plan around them.

money.title: What you could keep
money.withSpend: At about {weekly} a week, six weeks adds up to around {sixWeeks} you could keep.
money.withGoal: That would get you to {savingFor} ({target}) in about {weeks} weeks.

onboarding._insights: The short 'something to know' cards shown between onboarding questions. Each choice can have its own card; people see the cards for the first one or two things they tapped (in the order they tapped them). 'fallback' shows when nothing they picked has a card. PLACEHOLDER wording until a psychologist has reviewed it.

questionnaire._note: PLACEHOLDER questions modelled on the PGSI. Before launch, check the licence for the real PGSI wording and have a psychologist approve these. Answers are stored privately and never shown as a diagnosis.
questionnaire.intro: In the last 12 months, how often...
items: ...have you bet more than you could really afford to lose?
...have you needed to bet larger amounts to get the same feeling?
...have you gone back another day to try to win back money you lost?
...have you borrowed money or sold something to gamble?
...have you felt you might have a problem with gambling?
...has gambling caused you health problems, including stress or anxiety?
...have people criticised your betting or said you had a problem?
...has your gambling caused money problems for you or your household?
...have you felt guilty about the way you gamble, or what happens when you gamble?

sos._readme: Urge SOS. 'breathingAudioUrl' is the guided breathing recording (null until one is uploaded). The breathing guide counts in and out in seconds. 'buddyMessage' is the text that opens ready to send to their buddy; they can change it before sending.
sos.intro: Urges are like waves. They build, peak and pass, usually within half an hour. You don't have to act on this one. Let's ride it out together.
sos.buddyMessage: Hey, I'm having a tough moment right now. Could you give me a call or send me a message?
